name: Arash Adel
title: Assistant Professor; Director, Adel Research Group
department: School of Architecture; Core Faculty, Princeton Robotics; Associated Faculty, Computer Science
fitReason: Strong substantive AI and physical-robot fit despite an Architecture appointment: simulation-trained diffusion policies, force-aware adaptive execution and full-scale contact-rich assembly are central current research methods.

physicalEvidence.summary: August 2026 primary study trains diffusion policies in Isaac Sim and deploys them on a physical six-axis UR20 with flange force/torque sensing and a custom pneumatic parallel gripper, handling combined payloads of 6–15.2 kg. It tests timber joinery, pipe fitting and sequential full-scale truss assembly. An L1-inspired adaptive controller corrects predicted actions online. Zero-shot means no task-specific policy fine-tuning with physical demonstrations; online adaptive correction remains active. Sequential assembly uses separately trained subtask policies, not one general-purpose construction policy.

shortVisit.summary: Current ARG team page advertises postdoctoral roles and Architecture PhD admissions with December 30, 2026 deadline. It does not publish an external master’s short-visitor route. Princeton’s current robotics seminar listing confirms Assistant Professor, core robotics and associated CS roles; the team roster names the two lead researchers of the 2026 physical study.
